records.name: AI-on-the-edge-device
records.summary: An ESP32-CAM project that reads existing water, gas or electricity meters and publishes the readings digitally.

assessment.reason: It adds digital reporting to a meter that already works. The value is in avoiding replacement hardware and extracting more use from the equipment you already have.
aiCantDo: Mount the camera rigidly in front of the real meter
Create stable lighting and remove glare from the physical installation
Choose and adjust the final camera angle and distance
Verify that the recognised reading matches the actual meter over time
assessment.mainCatch: Mounting, lighting and camera alignment are part of the system. Recognition software cannot compensate for a poor physical installation.

records.name: Circular Knitic
records.summary: An open hardware circular knitting machine built with 3D printed parts, laser-cut acrylic, Arduino control and conventional knitting needles.

assessment.reason: This is exactly the kind of project that broadens AI-assisted making beyond electronics. The machine itself is physical textile fabrication, while AI can help adapt patterns, parametric parts, control logic and obsolete sourcing.
assessment.mainCatch: The source is mature rather than current, and it explicitly depends on precise high-quality printing plus large 5mm and 6mm acrylic parts. Mechanical accuracy is the project.

records.name: Clawd Mochi
records.summary: A small ESP32-C3 desk companion with animated faces, web controls and a published low-cost parts list.

assessment.reason: Cheap, compact and easy to modify. It is a good example of AI-assisted embedded work becoming approachable without turning into a large electronics project.
aiCantDo: Wire the display to the ESP32-C3 correctly
Route and secure the electronics inside the case
Judge whether the finished object looks and feels tidy enough to keep on a desk
assessment.mainCatch: The concept is simple enough that finish quality matters. A rough print and untidy wiring quickly make it feel like a prototype.

records.name: ESP32 Air Quality Monitor
records.summary: A small ESP32 instrument showing temperature, humidity, pressure and a comfort label on an OLED display.

assessment.reason: It is a low-risk first sensor build with a useful result and obvious expansion routes into logging, Wi-Fi, automation and more visible indicators.
aiCantDo: Place the sensor where heat and poor airflow do not bias the reading
Wire and power the I2C devices correctly
Check the displayed values against real room conditions
Design a ventilated enclosure that does not compromise the measurement
assessment.mainCatch: Sensor placement affects the measurement. Putting the BME280 beside heat-producing electronics or sealing it in an unventilated enclosure undermines the result.

records.name: Gridfinity Rebuilt
records.summary: A parametric OpenSCAD implementation of Gridfinity bins with configurable sizes, compartments, tabs, bases and print options.

assessment.reason: It converts a useful storage standard into something configurable. AI can help generate or modify parameter sets without turning every custom bin into a CAD exercise.
aiCantDo: Measure the real drawer, shelf and objects
Print the physical bins and baseplates
Check fit and tolerances on the actual printer
Decide whether the finished storage arrangement is convenient in use
assessment.mainCatch: The design work is easy compared with print time. Large storage systems consume more filament and machine hours than the first few bins suggest.

records.name: ImageGenCam
records.summary: A buildable Raspberry Pi camera designed around a Codex-assisted hardware and software workflow.

assessment.reason: There is no obvious finished-product equivalent. The point is the combination of custom hardware, image generation and a build process that deliberately gives an AI coding agent meaningful work.
assessment.mainCatch: The software is only half the product. Enclosure quality, assembly and camera ergonomics still decide whether the result feels finished.

records.name: Morning Thermal Printer
records.summary: An ESP32 desk printer that turns weather and calendar data into a short physical morning briefing on receipt paper.

assessment.reason: It is a clean example of software and public data becoming a physical ritual object. The hardware is modest, while the useful customisation lives in what the device fetches and prints.
assessment.mainCatch: The thermal printer needs its own stable 5V supply. Powering it from the ESP32 regulator is specifically warned against because the print head current causes brownouts.

records.name: OpenFlexure Microscope
records.summary: A 3D-printable microscope platform with precise flexure-based sample positioning and multiple optical configurations.

assessment.reason: It provides a serious open instrument platform rather than a classroom toy, with the option to change mechanics, optics and automation.
assessment.mainCatch: Optics, calibration and precise assembly matter more than simply getting the printed parts to fit together.

records.name: OpenMower
records.summary: A conversion that replaces the electronics in compatible robot mowers with GPS-guided, map-aware open hardware and software.

assessment.reason: It can turn a compatible basic mower into a much more capable open platform. The case is strongest if you value control, mapping and modification rather than simply needing the grass cut.
assessment.mainCatch: This is a substantial machine conversion involving electronics, Linux, mechanical work and outdoor safety. AI does not remove the consequences of getting those parts wrong.

records.name: OpenScan Mini
records.summary: A compact open-source photogrammetry scanner that rotates small objects through controlled camera positions to create detailed 3D models.

assessment.reason: It turns physical objects into reusable digital geometry with an unusually accessible open hardware route. AI can help with scan preparation, photogrammetry workflow, cleanup and adapting the printable frame.
assessment.mainCatch: Scan quality still depends on lighting, surface preparation, focus, object positioning and photogrammetry processing. The hardware does not make every object easy to scan.

records.name: PAROL6 Desktop Robot Arm
records.summary: A six-axis open desktop robot arm with printable structure, a published BOM, control electronics, GUI, Python API and ROS2/MoveIt routes.

assessment.reason: It is a serious robotics platform rather than a novelty arm. The open mechanics, control stack, Python API and ROS2 ecosystem give AI useful software work after the physical machine is correctly assembled.
assessment.mainCatch: This is a high-consequence multi-axis machine. The source carries explicit serious-hazard warnings, and calibration, wiring, power, joint assembly and safe testing remain human responsibilities.

records.name: Sesame Robot
records.summary: A printable ESP32 quadruped using eight servos, an expressive OLED face and open animation/control software.

assessment.reason: The result is a useful robotics platform rather than a one-off novelty. Hardware, movement, expressions and software can all be changed after the first build.
assessment.mainCatch: Eight servos, printed mechanics and wiring create plenty of opportunities for small errors to become movement problems.

records.name: SmartKnob
records.summary: An open haptic control knob that uses a brushless gimbal motor and magnetic encoder to create software-defined detents, endstops, springs and other tactile behaviours.

assessment.reason: It is an unusually capable physical interface whose feel is defined in software. AI can help understand the control code, create behaviours and debug integrations, but the value only appears after a difficult electronics and mechanical build works reliably.
assessment.cost: No stable complete build price published
aiCantDo: Reflow or hot-air solder fine-pitch components
assessment.mainCatch: The creator explicitly says SmartKnob View is not a mature plug-and-play project. It requires very small-pitch surface-mount soldering, delicate assembly and an expectation of hardware and firmware troubleshooting.
